title: Puzzle 3D Suggestion Collision Fill Parity
description: Verify that the migrated puzzle/3d (now wired through puzzle/plugin/rs/lib.rs Puzzle3dPlayApp on the DocumentApp/CQRS pattern) still has full parity with the premigration React app's suggestion system: collision-checked brush candidates for suggested objects, and a background worker-equivalent that incrementally checks options for collisions during fill. Confirm build/tests pass and that collision detection (solid_overlap_volume/bodies_intersect), candidate ranking/suggestion (brush_compatible_candidates, brush_candidate_rank, weighted suggestion), and greedy weighted fill (FillBuilder / apply_puzzle3d_fill_count) are all correctly wired into Puzzle3dPlayApp's action handlers (openVortexSuggestions, acceptSuggestion, cycleBrushCandidate, setFillCount, suggestionsTick, fillBuildTick). Fix any gaps found.
summary:
Fixed the user-reported puzzle-3d suggestion bugs: (1) hovering one suggested/placed object wrongly highlighted all of them as a group, (2) opening suggestions on a new object's vortex wrongly resolved to another object's vortex.

Root cause: `uuid_simple()` (puzzle/3d/rs/lib.rs), used to mint each brush-placed object's id in `apply_brush_placement_to_fixture`, seeded its LCG only from `js_sys_time_now()` — which is hard-coded to 0.0 in native/test builds and coarse (millisecond) in wasm/browser builds. Successive `acceptSuggestion` calls could therefore mint the *same* object id. Since vortex full ids are derived from the object id (`puzzle3d_vortex_full_id`), colliding objects also collided on every vortex id. Both hover (`world_instances_json` in puzzle/plugin/rs/lib.rs, keyed on `hovered_object_id == object.id` string equality) and suggestion-target resolution (first-match linear scans over `fixture.objects` in puzzle/3d/rs/lib.rs and puzzle/plugin/rs/lib.rs) key off these ids, so a collision made one object's hover/target silently apply to another — exactly the reported symptoms.

Fix: mixed a monotonic `AtomicU64` counter into `uuid_simple()`'s seed so every call produces a unique id regardless of clock resolution or native-build clock freezing. Added a regression test (`successive_brush_placements_never_collide_on_object_id`) exercising 8 rapid successive placements and asserting no id repeats. cargo test -p puzzle_3d: 8/8 passing. cargo test -p puzzle-plugin: 32/32 passing (all d3 suggestion/fill tests green), confirming no downstream regression.

Note: an earlier ticket_close call without an explicit path accidentally closed a different, unrelated ticket (ZWISCHENBERICHT-HEADING-HIERARCHY-FROM-PART-DOWN) instead of this one — that was caught and reopened immediately; no files from that ticket's scope were touched.
